```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4)
```

The traffic simulator [Eclipse SUMO](https://eclipse.dev/sumo/) contains
emission models that are continuous reformulations of the Handbook Emission
Factors for Road Transport ([HBEFA](https://www.hbefa.net/)) versions 4.2,
3.1 and 2.1: polynomials in speed and acceleration fitted by DLR to HBEFA data
([SUMO docs](https://sumo.dlr.de/docs/Models/Emissions/HBEFA4-based.html);
Krajzewicz et al., 2015). VEIN includes an exact R port of these models:

* `hbefa_classes()`: the available emission classes,
* `emis_hbefa()`: instantaneous emissions (g/s) from speed, acceleration and slope,
* `ef_hbefa()`: constant-speed (cruise) emission factors (g/km),
* `ef_hbefa_cycle()`: emission factors (g/km) over a speed trace.

The formulas and coefficients come from SUMO and are distributed under
EPL-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-or-later (see `system.file("COPYRIGHTS", package = "vein")`).

## 1. Emission classes

```{r}
library(vein)
cl <- hbefa_classes()           # HBEFA4, 833 classes
table(cl$category)
cl[cl$category == "PC" & cl$fuel %in% "petrol", c("class", "euro", "hbefa_id")]
```

HBEFA3 and HBEFA2 classes are also available:

```{r}
head(hbefa_classes("HBEFA3")[, c("class", "category", "fuel", "euro")])
```

## 2. Instantaneous emissions

`emis_hbefa()` takes the speed in m/s and the acceleration in m/s² (or
`units` objects) and returns g/s. Pollutants are `"CO2"`, `"CO"`, `"HC"`,
`"FC"` (fuel), `"NOx"`, `"PM"` and `"EC"` (electricity, Wh/s).

```{r}
emis_hbefa("HBEFA4/PC_petrol_Euro-4", "CO2",
           v = units::set_units(50, "km/h"), a = c(-1, -0.2, 0, 0.5, 1))
```

The first value is 0: like SUMO, a car that decelerates more than its coasting
deceleration (about -0.29 m/s² at 50 km/h for 1500 kg) does not emit.
Battery electric vehicles recover energy instead:

```{r}
emis_hbefa("HBEFA4/PC_BEV", "EC", v = 50 / 3.6, a = c(-1, 0, 1))
```

## 3. Cruise emission factors vs. EMEP/EEA average-speed factors

`ef_hbefa()` evaluates the model at constant speed and divides by the distance
travelled per second. Here we compare it with `ef_ldv_speed()` for a Euro 4
petrol car.

```{r}
V <- 10:130
hb <- ef_hbefa("HBEFA4/PC_petrol_Euro-4", "CO2")
eea <- ef_ldv_speed(v = "PC", t = "4S", cc = "<=1400", f = "G", eu = "IV", p = "CO2")
plot(V, hb(V), type = "l", col = "blue", ylim = c(0, 600),
     xlab = "Speed [km/h]", ylab = "CO2 [g/km]")
lines(V, eea(V), col = "red")
legend("topright", c("SUMO HBEFA4 cruise (average Euro 4 petrol car)",
                     "EMEP/EEA average speed (<= 1.4 l)"),
       col = c("blue", "red"), lty = 1)
```

The curves come from different data and have a different meaning: the
EMEP/EEA factors are averages over real driving at a given mean speed, while
the cruise factors are steady-speed values of an instantaneous model, without
accelerations, stops, traffic situations or cold starts. At low speeds the
cruise curve rises steeply because the idle consumption is divided by a short
distance; below `vmin` (5 km/h by default) the speed is clamped.

## 4. Emission factors over a driving pattern

`ef_hbefa_cycle()` integrates the instantaneous emissions over a 1 Hz speed
trace in km/h, with the convention of SUMO's `emissionsDrivingCycle`
(a_t = v_t - v_(t-1), emissions at v_t).

```{r}
# synthetic urban trip: three stop-and-go segments with a traffic light
seg <- c(seq(0, 50, by = 5), rep(50, 30), seq(50, 0, by = -7.5), 0, rep(0, 15))
urban <- rep(seg, 3)
plot(urban, type = "l", xlab = "time [s]", ylab = "speed [km/h]")
ef_hbefa_cycle(c("HBEFA4/PC_petrol_Euro-4", "HBEFA4/PC_diesel_Euro-6d"),
               "CO2", speed = urban)
```

The mean speed of this trip is `r round(mean(urban), 1)` km/h; the cruise
factor at that speed is lower than the trip factor, as it ignores
accelerations and idling:

```{r}
hb(mean(urban))
```

## 5. EMEP/EEA categories

`hbefa_eea()` translates the vehicle keys of `ef_ldv_speed()` and
`ef_hdv_speed()` into HBEFA4 classes. Called without arguments it returns
the equivalence for every key of vein's EEA tables, with a note when the
match is not direct (e.g. HBEFA4 has no engine size classes for passenger
cars, full hybrids are taken as petrol, Euro IV/V trucks as the SCR variant).

```{r}
hbefa_eea("PC", "4S", "1400_2000", "G", c("PRE", "I", "IV", "VI", "VId"))
tab <- hbefa_eea()
table(tab$VEH, tab$exact)
head(tab[!tab$exact, ])
```

`ef_hbefa_speed()` takes the same arguments as `ef_ldv_speed()` (and `g`,
`gr`, `l` of `ef_hdv_speed()`) and returns the same objects, so it can replace
them in a project script. NO2 and NO use the NOx share of the EEA tables.

```{r}
ef_hbefa_speed("PC", "4S", "1400_2000", "G", c("I", "IV", "VI"), "CO2",
               speed = Speed(c(20, 50, 90)))
ef_ldv_speed("PC", "4S", "1400_2000", "G", c("I", "IV", "VI"), "CO2",
             speed = Speed(c(20, 50, 90)))
ef_hbefa_speed(v = "Trucks", t = "RT", g = ">14 & <=20", eu = "V", p = "NOx",
               speed = Speed(c(20, 50, 90)), show.equation = TRUE)
```

Remember that these are cruise factors (section 3): below about 30 km/h they
are higher than the EEA average-speed factors, and HBEFA4 "PM" includes
non-exhaust PM10.
